title: A holder checkpoints its item: head, branch and a bounded working-tree diff

story.i_want_to: record on the item what I did, what is next, the head I pushed and my uncommitted diff
story.so_that: whoever takes the item over reads its record and checks out that state instead of reconstructing it from a branch, a transcript or a prose handoff

rationale: PRD R1: 'A holder checkpoints to the item while it works ... Uncommitted work travels through loopctl.' Today nothing can hold it: a release clears the head the runner reported (StageMachine.clears/3, lib/loopctl/delivery/stage_machine.ex:938, @released_clears :522), a stage event's data is capped at 8,000 bytes (stages.ex:201), and the only carrier of 'where I left off' is a free-text handoff post capped at 16 KiB (channel_post.ex:97). This story adds the one record a move (US-52.43) ships and a puller (US-52.44, US-52.46) applies.

acceptance_criteria.description: A table story_checkpoints (schema Loopctl.Delivery.StoryCheckpoint, context Loopctl.Delivery.Checkpoints, RLS enabled) holds id (client-supplied uuid), tenant_id, story_id, holder_id, claim_epoch, branch, head_sha, diff (bytea, nullable), diff_bytes, diff_sha256, wip_branch (nullable), fenced (default false), summary (nullable), resolution, resolved_by_holder_id, resolved_at and inserted_at, with a CHECK that octet_length(diff) is at most Checkpoints.max_diff_bytes/0 and an index on (tenant_id, story_id, inserted_at DESC); tenant_id, holder_id, claim_epoch and fenced are set by the context, never cast.

Checkpoints.record/4 (tenant_id, story_id, holder, attrs) by the item's current holder (stories.assigned_holder_id equals holder.id, the presented claim_epoch is the story's, the claim lease not run out) inserts an unfenced checkpoint, writes attrs done and next as one progress note on the item, and appends a checkpointed event naming the checkpoint id, head_sha and diff_bytes, all in one transaction under the story row lock.

A diff longer than Checkpoints.max_diff_bytes/0 (the bound_bytes US-52.40 recorded) is refused {:error, {:diff_over_bound, max}}, rendered 413 code diff_over_bound with max_diff_bytes and the message 'The working-tree diff is <n> bytes and the bound is <max>. Commit the work to a branch named wip/..., push it, and checkpoint with wip_branch instead of diff.'; nothing is stored.

A checkpoint may carry wip_branch matching ^wip/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]{1,200}$ instead of a diff and is stored with diff null; one carrying both is refused 422 code diff_and_wip_branch, and a wip_branch outside the pattern 422 code invalid_wip_branch.
A diff in which an added line matches Loopctl.Security.SecretDenylist.contains_secret?/1 is refused 422 code secret_in_diff naming the files whose added lines matched, and nothing is stored.

A record retried with the same checkpoint id and byte-identical content returns the stored row with replayed: true and writes no second note or event; the same id with different content is refused 409 code checkpoint_id_conflict.

A caller that has never held the item at any claim_epoch (no claim event in the item's log names its holder) is refused 409 code not_holder naming the current holder's id, kind and host, and a story of another tenant is 404.

POST /api/v1/stories/:id/checkpoints (exact_role: :agent) records one; GET /api/v1/stories/:id/checkpoints (role: :agent, newest first, at most 20, metadata only) and GET /api/v1/stories/:id/checkpoints/:checkpoint_id (diff base64) read them; MCP tools work_item_checkpoint (which computes the diff itself from a worktree argument) and work_item_checkpoints reach them, with README rows and a wiring test.

test_cases.name: the current holder records a checkpoint, a progress note and an event in one transaction (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant = fixture(:tenant); story claimed by holder = fixture(:holder) (provided by US-52.13) at claim_epoch e
steps: Checkpoints.record(tenant.id, story.id, holder, %{id: uuid, claim_epoch: e, branch: "feature/x", head_sha: sha, diff: diff, done: "wired the route", next: "tests"})
expected_results: one row fenced false, diff_sha256 of diff; one progress note; one checkpointed event naming the row

test_cases.name: bound, wip_branch and their refusals (DataCase + ConnCase)
steps: record a diff of max_diff_bytes() + 1 bytes
expected_results: {:error, {:diff_over_bound, max}} and no row; a row with diff nil; 422 diff_and_wip_branch; 422 invalid_wip_branch; 413 diff_over_bound with max_diff_bytes

test_cases.name: a credential in an added line is refused; one in a removed line is not (DataCase)
preconditions: a diff adding `TOKEN=lc_live_0123456789abcdef` to config/dev.exs; a second diff removing that line

test_cases.name: replay and id conflict (DataCase)
steps: record the same id with another diff
expected_results: replayed: true, one note, one event; {:error, :checkpoint_id_conflict}

test_cases.name: a stranger and another tenant are refused (DataCase)
preconditions: story held by H1; holder H2 of the same agent that never claimed it; tenant B with a holder
steps: record as the tenant-B holder on tenant A's story id

test_cases.name: routes and role gates (ConnCase)
preconditions: holder credential; a user key; an orchestrator key
steps: GET the list as the user key
expected_results: 201; 403 (exact_role :agent); 200 newest first with no diff field; 200 with diff base64

test_cases.name: work_item_checkpoint computes the diff from a worktree (node --test)
preconditions: mcp-server/test with a temp git repo: pushed branch, a tracked edit, an untracked file; stubbed fetch
expected_results: POST body head_sha = the pushed head, diff covers the edit and the untracked file, the repo's index is unchanged; tool declared and dispatched

technical_notes: Why a new table: story_stages keeps one current value per identity and clears head_sha on every release (stage_machine.ex:499-506, 522); story_stage_events.data is capped at 8,000 bytes (stages.ex:201) and is the log, not the payload; story_notes (provided by release 3, README names table: work-item notes) are text sections; channel_posts are messages (US-52.22). A checkpoint is head + branch + a binary diff up to the measured bound, kept as state on the item (PRD section 7 point 1).

Checkpoints.max_diff_bytes/0 is a module attribute holding bound_bytes from docs/factory/measurements/release-7.md (US-52.40); the migration's CHECK and the refusal read the same value (CLAUDE.md, Doc hygiene: one attribute for an enforced and documented limit). Add the 413 and every 422/409 code to the operation/2 spec.

head_sha is the commit the diff applies to: the branch's pushed head, or the base commit when the branch was never pushed; diff = `git diff --binary <head_sha>` over a temporary index with untracked, non-ignored files added intent-to-add (the shape US-52.40 measured). The MCP tool shares that code with US-52.46 in mcp-server/lib/worktree-diff.js; mcp-server already runs git locally (mcp-server/lib/client-context.js:45,67).

Holder identity is release 3's: stories.assigned_holder_id and the holder on the authenticating key (US-52.14 AC-52.14.1; Loopctl.Holders, US-52.13). Epoch and lease checks reuse Progress.check_claim_epoch/3 (lib/loopctl/progress.ex:2282) and the claim's claimed_until. 'Ever held' reads the claim events release 3 writes with actor_holder_id (README names table: work-item event log).

Secret scan: SecretDenylist.contains_secret?/1 (lib/loopctl/security/secret_denylist.ex:116) over each added (+) line, grouped by the file header; the same denylist channel posts and claims use (channel_claim.ex:297).

Role gates: write exact_role: :agent like claim and renew (story_status_controller.ex:59-61), so only a holder credential writes; reads role: :agent, so fleet_dash's user key reads (README user journey). New MCP tools carry what they refuse in their descriptions (CLAUDE.md, An operator-facing endpoint is NOT DONE until an MCP tool calls it).
non_goals: Checkpoints from a late holder, resolving them, and pruning: US-52.42.
Shipping a checkpoint with a move and applying it on the target: US-52.43, US-52.44, US-52.46.
Runner sessions checkpointing from the host daemon: US-52.44.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.41.6: a holder that loses loopctl mid-write retries the same checkpoint id on reconnect and gets the stored row, never a second checkpoint; a late retry after its claim ended is US-52.42's fenced path.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.41.1: the checkpoint lives in story_checkpoints in loopctl's Postgres; the worktree is a copy, so a crashed session loses only what it never checkpointed.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.41.6: the client-supplied id dedupes a retry; different content under one id is refused, never overwritten.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.41.3: the diff is bounded, so one checkpoint request is at most the measured size; over it the holder pushes a WIP branch instead.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.41.8: the checkpoint is written by the holder through the API or its MCP tool, wherever the holder runs, and read by any holder or fleet_dash by story id.

defaults: List read: newest 20 checkpoints, metadata only.
WIP branch pattern: wip/<anything branch-safe>, at most 204 characters.
definition_of_done: From an MCP session holding a sandbox item: work_item_checkpoint on a worktree with one edit returns 201, and GET /api/v1/stories/:id/checkpoints/:checkpoint_id returns a diff that `git apply --check` accepts on a clean checkout of head_sha.
